rename.to: [Ivy] customElements.define fails when in Module constructor

body:
Just a quick note that the issue occurs because `customElements.define('test-ce', headerCE);` happens in the `TestModule` constructor and is unrelated to `Optional` DI.

The failure chain is 
1. `AppModule` instantiates and starts creating a root injector 
2. during root injector creation, hydrate `TestModule` 
3. `TestModule` defines `TestComponent` customElement 
4. Angular Elements attempts to instantiate root component for `TestComponent`
5. `TestComponent` attempts to inject `Router`
6. Try to retrieve `Router` from injector that hasn't been created yet

Yeah, mentioned something similar in the description under the last bullet. This works with ng8 though, we had that code in production already. I'm not very good with internals of angular, but if I understood correctly, it's some kind of race condition which was not happening in ng8? Perhaps it is just no longer a valid way to use `customElements.define`?

Right, the difference you're observing between v8 and v9 is that v9 would enable Ivy by default which is a completely different runtime than before (including the injector implementation). The injector was instantiated in a more incremental way in the previous runtime (https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/core/src/view/refs.ts#L374-L379) - `injector = this` followed by pushing to providers in `initNgModule`.

I'm still investigating if there's something that can be done about this in Ivy. Your proposed workaround of moving the `customElements.define` to `ngDoBootstrap` seems correct and reasonable in the meantime.
This will likely be fixed by https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/35731

issue.body:
This is a follow up to #35637 which resolved a similar issue for `ComponentFactoryResolver`, but not the root cause. When a `NgModuleRef` is created, it instantiates an `Injector` internally which in turn resolves all of injector types. This can result in a circular call that results in an error, because the module is one of the injector types being resolved.

These changes work around the issue by allowing the constructor to run before resolving the injector types.

Fixes #35677.
Fixes #35639.

issue.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package The issue is probably caused by package @angular/core, but regards the lazy loading feature for Module. So it could be a compiler thing with loadChildren? ### Is this a regression? Cant really tell from own experience but according to: https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/35402 https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/35576 which both seem to be related, i would probably say yes. ### Description To give some more background information: We are using feature modules as packages and bundling these into an application to expose them as angular elements. When using these angular elements (web-components) in any other application everything works fine. So now we started migrating our application towards a new workspace where we could integrate these feature libraries and while doing so we are lazy loading the modules to improve performance. So basically its not possible to lazy load any libraries/packages from your node_modules, therefor you have to create a small wrapper module. So we did that and use a component to render our feature. The strange thing is, if we render our angular element (web-component) everything works perfect, angular doesnt try to do smart things and the providers are available including our config. But as soon as we start to render the angular component variant, it throws error about providers that are missing. We define our providers inside of our feature module with the providers array syntax. We are aware of the `@Injectable({ providedIn })` options, but none of these work for us. ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction Because of the size i can not include any example of the current setup but i could try to make a small repro ASAP. But to give at least a bit of code/error context here is some pseudo code: ```ts // The module from our library/package @NgModule({ declarations: [FeatureComponent], entryComponents: [FeatureComponent], exports: [FeatureComponent], providers: [FeatureService], }) export class FeatureModule {} // The component from our library/package @Component({ selector: 'feature-component', template: `

Hello World!

`, }) export class FeatureComponent { constructor(private featureService: FeatureService) {} } // The lazy loaded module in the app @NgModule({ declarations: [LazyFeatureComponent], imports: [FeatureModule], }) export class LazyFeatureModule {} // The lazy loaded component in the app @Component({ selector: 'lazy-feature-component', template: ``, }) export class LazyFeatureComponent {} ``` ## 🔥 Exception or Error We use loadChildren to target the wrapper module from the app so it loads the feature module from the package. But when we navigate to this route we get the following error: ``` ERROR NullInjectorError: StaticInjectorError(AppModule)[FeatureComponent -> FeatureService]: StaticInjectorError(Platform: core)[FeatureComponent-> FeatureService]: NullInjectorError: No provider for FeatureService! ``` Which is very strange because we define our providers in the FeatureModule that is imported in the LazyFeatureModule. So it always should have the correct providers when importing it. Also the error refers to AppModule, so the FeatureComponent is not part of the FeatureModule but the AppModule/ which it shouldn't be part of. ### Workaround If we use angular elements and put the web-component tag inside of the LazyFeatureComponent everything works fine :) Somehow the module gets properly isolated and the providers are included as expected. ## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:**
